name: Asylum (Affirmative, I-589)
summary: Affirmative asylum and withholding of removal application filed with USCIS, including spouse and unmarried children under 21 as derivatives.
confidentialityNote: Asylum application information is confidential under 8 CFR 208.6. Do not disclose to third parties without written consent.

forms.title: Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal
Additional information / why corroboration is unavailable

filing.where: If not in immigration court: mail as shown on uscis.gov/i-589. If in removal proceedings, file with the Immigration Court instead (not this preset).
filing.fee: See Form G-1055 at uscis.gov/g-1055 (I-589 Instructions 07/28/26, section VIII).

questions.label: Native language and other languages you speak fluently
Why are you seeking protection? (choose all that apply: race, religion, nationality, political opinion, membership in a particular social group, torture)
Have you, your family or close friends ever been harmed, mistreated or threatened? Describe what happened, when, who did it and why.
Do you fear harm if you return? Who would harm you and why?
Groups, parties or organizations you or your family belonged to in your home country
Countries you passed through or lived in before coming to the U.S., and whether you applied for protection there
Include your spouse in the U.S. as a derivative?
Number of children you have (any age, anywhere)
Your brothers and sisters (names, cities and countries of residence)
Your last address in the country where you fear persecution, and address history for the last 5 years before coming

checklist.label: Your written personal declaration (staff will help you write it)
checklist.help: We build it with you from your intake answers. Upload any notes or drafts you have.

checklist.label: Copy of every passport or travel document you have, cover to cover
U.S. immigration documents (Form I-94, parole papers, notices)
Other identity documents (birth certificate, national ID card, driver's license)
Marriage certificate (and proof prior marriages ended)
Birth certificates or school records for each child included
Evidence of what happened to you (police reports, medical records, photos, threats, membership cards, witness letters)
checklist.help: If you cannot get this evidence, tell us why. USCIS requires an explanation (Supplement B).

checklist.label: Country conditions reports and news articles
checklist.help: Staff gather reports for the country of feared persecution.

checklist.label: Health professional's report (if it is hard for you to talk about past harm)
Police and court records for any arrest or charge

coverLetter.re: Form I-589, Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal
coverLetter.request: We respectfully submit the enclosed Form I-589 on behalf of {{givenName}} {{familyName}}, a national of {{citizenship}}, seeking asylum, withholding of removal, and protection under the Convention Against Torture.
points: The applicant suffered past persecution and/or has a well-founded fear of future persecution.
The harm is on account of a protected ground: {{grounds}}.
The application is filed within one year of the applicant's last arrival, or an exception applies.
Corroborating evidence is enclosed; where it is not reasonably available, the reason is explained.

assemblyNote: I-589 Instructions 07/28/26, section X: original I-589 first, then supplementary sheets, supporting documentation, then relationship evidence. Attorney decides whether the cover letter goes on top.
